merger_name: Telstra – indefeasible rights over dark fibre on Tabua, Proa and Bulikula subsea cables
merger_description:
Telstra International Networks Pty Ltd (**TINS**) and Telstra Australia Networks Pty Ltd (**TANS**), each a wholly owned subsidiary of Telstra Group Limited (**Telstra**), propose to acquire indefeasible rights of use (**IRUs**) over dark fibre on three new subsea cables (the Tabua, Proa and Bulikula cables (together, the **Pacific Connect Cables**)) from Manta Ray Solutions LLC and Perch Infrastructure Pty Ltd, being indirect subsidiaries of Google LLC (the **Acquisition**).

TINS and TANS supply international telecommunications services to government, enterprise and business customers outside Australia. In Australia, Telstra provides mobile, fixed-line, internet and data services to consumers, businesses and government, amongst other telecommunications and technology infrastructure.

Subsea cables are fibre-optic cables that carry telecommunications data (principally internet traffic, telephone calls, and private-network data) underwater between countries, continents and islands. The Pacific Connect Cables are high fibre count subsea systems, with each of those systems comprising 16 fibre pairs.

The subsea dark fibre being acquired by Telstra will need to be ‘lit’ by Telstra to enable live services. Telstra will need to install its own electronic equipment, known as submarine line termination equipment, to activate capacity on each of its designated fibre pairs. The IRUs to be acquired will provide Telstra with an exclusive right to use certain fibre pairs on the Pacific Connect Cables for a period of 15 years. Telstra will have the ability to sell some or all of the capacity that it activates on these cables to third parties.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. post-Acquisition, Telstra’s share of fibre pairs and/or
capacity on each of the Pacific Connect Cables and other
cables connected to Australia is expected to be small
b. there are alternative providers of subsea dark fibre and
capacity on subsea cables connected to Australia
c. the Acquisition is unlikely to foreclose access to the
remaining fibre pairs on the Pacific Connect Cables or to
capacity on alternative cables connected to Australia for
Telstra’s downstream rivals.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
